title: A Date with Judy
paragraphs: Teenage family situation comedy created by Aleen Leslie. Frozen GRH subset contains thirteen surviving objects from 1942-1949 and crosses Judy-performer, sponsor and network eras. One school-dance file carries a collector date of 1946-05-18 but the indexed broadcast is 1948-05-18; the frozen row is not rewritten.

GRH documents the program through NBC summer replacement years (June 24, 1941 to September 15, 1942) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], NBC Bristol-Myers summer run (June 30, 1943 to September 22, 1943) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], NBC Tums regular run (January 18, 1944 to January 4, 1949) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], and ABC final season (October 13, 1949 to May 4, 1950) on [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Aleen Leslie (creator on 13 recordings and writer on 12 recordings), [[person|john-brown|John Brown]] (performer on 12 recordings), Louise Erickson (performer on 12 recordings), Helen Mack (director on 9 recordings and producer on 9 recordings), Myra Marsh (performer on 9 recordings), Richard Crenna (performer on 8 recordings), and Dix Davis (performer on 7 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.66865a83f6609315|KFI]] (aircheck from station), [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network), and [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]] (rebroadcast by).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include family and generational comedy, teenage social life, dating and courtship, Hollywood celebrity culture, school and youth culture, and teen music and dance culture.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Rise of teenage-focused radio situation comedy, Move from NBC to ABC for final season, World War II home-front broadcasting, and 1948 MGM A Date with Judy film during radio popularity peak.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]] (13 shared credited people), [[show|the-great-gildersleeve|The Great Gildersleeve]] (7 shared credited people), [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]] (5 shared credited people), [[show|broadway-is-my-beat|Broadway Is My Beat]] (4 shared credited people), and [[show|duffys-tavern|Duffy's Tavern]] (4 shared credited people).
